claim_decisions.statement: A study of monthly weather and police records for 1,158 South African police wards in 2001-2012 reports warmer-month associations with violent crime and modest rural property-taking responses to growing-season drought, not urban crime. Effects are subtle, mediation is unidentified and weather findings do not establish anthropogenic climate attribution.

gaps: No source-stated climate-change-to-organized-conflict or conflict-to-adaptation mechanism was verified. Historical weather-crime associations do not identify a mediated pathway or anthropogenic climate effect.
The Cape Winelands local profile uses 1996/2011 social indicators, 2017 water data and modeled mid-century risks. It is not a current nationwide municipal comparison.
NDC legal and planning commitments are not evidence of compliance or delivered services. Workshop statements are not representative municipal or farmer surveys.
Some relevant BTR and World Bank PDFs exceeded the web reader's size limit; their indexed snippets were not used as evidence.

executive_assessment.text: Provincial climate impacts and household vulnerability differ, with water, sanitation and food poverty shaping sensitivity in named provinces.
Cape Winelands evidence identifies De Doorns, Touwsrivier and Witzenberg vulnerabilities, but the indicators are dated and future risks are modeled.

National mandates, municipal prioritization and community organizations provide an adaptation-readiness picture, not proof of delivered outcomes. Historical weather-crime associations remain causally and geographically bounded.
